name: Spawn Position
desc: Sets the player's spawn position (where compass points and respawn occurs).

writeup.p: Carries the world spawn as a packed BlockPos. ServerConfigurationManager sends it on player join (lines ~164 and ~476 in the bundled sources) and CommandSetDefaultSpawnpoint broadcasts it to all players when /setworldspawn runs (line ~45). The value drives the compass needle, the debug-screen spawn readout and the fallback respawn point; it is world metadata, not player state.

handleSpawnPosition runs on the main thread and performs two writes: thePlayer.setSpawnPoint(pos, true) (func_180473_a in MCP) for the personal bed spawn, and world.getWorldInfo().setSpawn(pos) for the world spawn. The packet never moves the player and touches no entity state, which is why nothing in the client reacts to it beyond the two field writes.

Zero module hits across all 8 clients; the only non-vanilla references are the Rise 6.x script whitelist entries (NetworkAPI.java line 51). Compass and waypoint features read mc.theWorld.getSpawnPoint() on render because the vanilla handler has already committed the value before any event bus runs, so intercepting S05 would only let a module lie to itself. There is no state transition in the packet for a module to key off.

None. A client-side mutation alters only the local compass and respawn UI, and the server re-sends the authoritative spawn on every join and respawn, so the change does not persist and cannot affect gameplay. No anti-cheat measures the packet.

implementation.overview: A one-field world-metadata write (BlockPos spawn) that the vanilla handler commits before any module event runs. Zero module hits in the 8-client corpus, so the module list is empty; compass and waypoint features read the committed value directly and have no reason to intercept the packet.
implementation.server_handling: ServerConfigurationManager sends S05PacketSpawnPosition on player join (line ~164 for the join sequence and line ~476 on respawn), and CommandSetDefaultSpawnpoint broadcasts it to all players when the spawn point changes. The BlockPos is packed as a single long on the wire. The server holds the authoritative copy and re-sends it at every world boundary, so a client-side alteration is always corrected within one join or respawn.
implementation.protocol_notes: Single BlockPos field encoded as one long (x << 38 | z << 12 | y in the 1.8 packing). Sent in the PLAY state, usually immediately after S01PacketJoinGame and before or alongside the initial chunk stream. Because the value feeds both the world info and the player's personal spawn, receiving it twice (join plus respawn) is normal and idempotent.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Nothing to flag: the packet carries no timing, position or input signal, and the client cannot send a serverbound equivalent. Its only downstream effect, the compass direction, has no anti-cheat relevance.
implementation.client_variations: All 8 clients ship the vanilla handler unchanged; Rise 6.x additionally whitelists the packet for the script API. Rise 5.99 has no corpus entry for this packet at all.
